steps.text: Rinse rice until the water runs clear; drain.

Heat coconut oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add rice and coconut flakes; cook and stir for 3 to 4 minutes. Stir in lime juice, then add coconut milk, chicken broth, lime zest, and salt. Bring to a low boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Remove from the heat and keep covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and season with pepper before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Lime Rice
raw_recipe.description: This easy coconut-lime rice has extra coconut flavor, thanks to coconut flakes and coconut milk, with the zest and juice of one lime adding a bright punch.

review.reviewBody: We had Coconut rice for the first time in San Francisco a couple of weeks ago. I searched for a recipe and came across this one. WOW!!! This was a big hit and came very close to what we had in San Fran other than I do not recall tasting the texture of the actual Coconut. That is one thing I would change next time around (I would chop the shredded Coconut very fine)... I also used Cocnut Cream in place of the Coconut milk which gave even a stronger Coconut taste (YUM)... We doubled the recipe and did serve with Cilantro... PERFECT DISH!!!! This one is going in the book. THANK YOU Karmabelle.

I have been making this recipe for over 10 years, easily! It’s what we want when we want Coconut Lime Rice. I have recently adapted it for the Instant Pot. I cook the rice and coconut on sauté mode in the butter and I use 1/2 TBSP of coconut oil instead of 1. I reduce the liquids to half their original specifications as I like how my rice turns out in the Instant Pot with a 1:1 ratio of rice and liquid. I also add fresh cilantro at the end when I fluff it with a fork. There have been plenty of times I’ve had it without cilantro and it’s still pretty great!

Made this last night and it was great. My changes: 
1. Use a cast iron skillet
2. Don't add coconut oil toast the rice - too oily at the end.
3. Use a whole can of coconut milk, 4 oz water, one chicken bullion cube.
4. Don't add extra salt - no need.

My husband and I both liked this recipe. The first time I made it I had problems with burning so the second time I used a burner that is even lower on the lowest setting. I used more coconut milk than chicken stock for a creamy result. I don't do low fat anything. This freezes well so I did not cut the batch down. I use fine shredded macaroon coconut. I find it hard to stop eating this!
One cup of rice for two sounded a little excessive; I quartered the recipe, and made it without the chicken broth... it was just PERFECT.

Didn't have Basmati rice , used jasmine rice instead. Followed directions, rinsing rice until water was clear. Put into a pan with Coconut oil & Earth Balance(soy free vegan butterey flavored spread) for 3-4 minutes. I Placed it in my rice cooker & added the rest of the ingredients. After my rice cooker's warming light came on , fluffed up the rice, and some lime zest sprinkled on it! I made an Indian curry to go with it. Absolutely delicious. I will definitely make it again.

This turned boring plain rice into the star of the meal! I served it with sauteed fresh veggies and grilled pork tenderloin. I did use a full teaspoon of salt and because my limes were small I used 3 of them. Will definitely make this again!

Excellent flavor. The zest will hold up better during cooking while the lime juice should be added at the end. Don't make the same mistake I did when using brown rice instead of white rice. I forgot that brown rice takes 40 minutes to cook not 20 minutes so it ended up holding up dinner!

Excellent dish! I've made this twice now. The first time I followed the recipe with the exception of adding everything into my rice cooker. It was perfect! The second time I had to improvise since I only had Jasmine rice and no coconut milk. I used an additional cup of chicken broth and a little extra coconut oil instead of butter and extra (sweetened)coconut flakes. Then I just dumped everything into the rice cooker without cooking it in a pan. I also forgot to add salt and pepper but it came out just as good and didn't need it. 
I cant express how good this recipe is even with missing ingredients!

I have made this twice now using Jasmine rice, a little more lime zest and juice. It is excellent! A permanent recipe in my collection. My daughter begged me to make it again; she couldn't stop eating it! Got ribs going in my pressure cooker with a spicy honey sauce. Can't wait for dinner.

Excellent recipe, easy to make and full of flavor. I used coconut cream instead of coconut milk as that is what I had available. I also added a little minced cilantro at the end. Fabulous! Will definitely be making again.
Perfect pairing with Thai peanut chicken.
This was amazing! Foldable the directions and it will go very well with a nice fish.
Made this in a rice cooker, added the ingredients towards the end of the rice being done, turned out beautifully, full of flavor!
Perfect recipe - made it to serve with Brazilian Moqueca fish stew recipe in July 2025 Cooking Light. Both recipes taste just like the originals sampled while in Brazil!

I have been on the hunt for a restaurant quality coconut lime rice recipe and this is it!! So easy and flavorful. I have experimented with trying to replicate something on my own, but I think the combination of chicken broth AND coconut milk here was the trick. Plus the sauteed coconut flakes doesn't hurt either. I was making this for a potluck, so I topped with chopped cilantro. I'm very pleased with this recipe!!
I made this tonight , the only change I made was adding fresh cilantro . It was fantastic, I’ve made recipes similar but this is the best one . A keeper for sure
I didn't use any chicken broth just 2 cups coconut milk. It's cooking now and I'm waiting to see how it comes out. Sounds good though.
Made this with no changes to go with an Asian chicken; awesome! I will make this a go-to recipe
